reasons: The cited grant in p0054 is squarely a deviation: the Deliverable licence is revocable, non-transferable, term-limited to the Order Form, and omits Affiliates and contractors — matching the rule's walk-away description.

The redline applies only the rule's targeted fixes (delete 'revocable'/'non-transferable', make it perpetual/irrevocable/fully paid, add Affiliates and contractors acting on Customer's behalf, add Affiliate/successor transfer cross-referenced to Section 13.3) and leaves Vendor's ownership sentence and the 'use a Deliverable' scope intact, so it is directionally correct and does not over-reach beyond the preferred position.

The two failed minimal-edit checks (ratios 0.78/0.85) are explained by the brevity of the one-sentence grant: almost every operative element of that sentence is a term the rule requires changing, so the high ratio reflects sentence length rather than scope creep; no unrelated concessions were extracted.

The comment is concise, first-person plural, states what changed and why, cites the internal consistency with Sections 13.1–13.3, and offers the playbook fallback (Affiliates on written notice; transfer limited to an M&A successor), consistent with tone requirements.
Severity 'high' is appropriate given the clause sits at the walk-away line for work product Customer paid to have created.
